issues.description: Shared TritonLoraConfig.is_registered is mutated from async request handlers without locking, creating a race and stale-cache hazard.
issues.detail: _create_trtllm_generate_request flips is_registered=True on a shared config returned by _get_lora_config. Concurrent first-requests can both see False and double-register, or a failed register can leave the flag True with no weights cached. Move registration state to a separate registry keyed by (model, task_id) with proper locking and a real backend-confirmed signal.

issues.description: lora_task_id is assigned positionally and can collide across model repositories, causing TRT-LLM to serve the wrong adapter.
issues.detail: task_id starts at 1 and increments per entry but resets per call and is not scoped per model. Two models with LoRAs get overlapping IDs, and TRT-LLM caches by task_id, so collisions can serve wrong weights. Derive task_id from a stable hash of (model, lora_name) or scope IDs explicitly per model.

issues.description: TritonLoraConfig collapses two distinct backend ADTs into one all-Optional dataclass, violating LSP.
issues.detail: vLLM only needs name; TRT-LLM requires task_id and path and mutates is_registered. Call sites like _create_trtllm_generate_request index fields the vLLM variant never sets. Split into a sealed hierarchy or tagged union (VllmLoraConfig, TrtllmLoraConfig) so required fields are non-Optional and substitution is total.

issues.description: Debug print and traceback.format_exc() calls left in production paths across the parser and FastAPI routers.
issues.detail: print(f"backend: {backend}") in the parse loop and unconditional print(traceback.format_exc()) in chat/completions/embeddings routers spam stdout, leak internals, and bypass the logger. Replace with logger calls at appropriate levels or remove; do not ship debug scaffolding as production behavior.

issues.description: _parse_lora_configs return-type annotation is stale (List[tuple[str,str]]) but actually returns List[TritonLoraConfig].
issues.detail: The signature is part of the contract and now misleads type checkers and future maintainers. Update to Optional[List[TritonLoraConfig]] or, better, return a typed LoraCatalog value object that also carries the backend kind so downstream code stops re-deriving it from a string flag.

issues.description: _parse_lora_configs is a 70-line backend-dispatching blob that should be split per backend.
issues.detail: One function handles vllm vs trtllm dispatch, path normalization, JSON parsing, file checks, and task_id assignment via a stringly-typed backend flag and nested try/except. Refactor into _parse_vllm_loras and _parse_trtllm_loras sharing a repo-walking helper, or a LoraCatalogProvider protocol per backend, so each branch is small and typed.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees this PR ships real correctness hazards behind a working happy path. The shared-mutable is_registered flag mutated from async handlers is a race and stale-cache bug, and positional lora_task_id assignment can collide across models and serve the wrong adapter via TRT-LLM's task_id cache. The TritonLoraConfig dataclass conflates two backend ADTs into one all-Optional shape, and the new _parse_lora_configs is a stringly-dispatched 70-line blob with a stale return annotation. Debug print and traceback calls leaked into production routers and must be removed. Needs-work before landing: split registration state from config, derive deterministic per-model task_ids, fix types, and strip debug scaffolding.
